SddReviewLifecycle.keywords: review-lifecycle, master, review-state, compress, publish, MR, external-review, git, gh, sdd-review-lifecycle
SddReviewLifecycle.Mission:
Drive a spec from review-state to merged master through EXTERNAL review. Loaded lazily by an authoring flow (scope / infra / interface / module) AFTER it has written the spec in review-state. I do NOT author spec content — the authoring flow did; I run the internal critic, publish the change for review, wait for the operator's verdict, and ONLY on approval compress + merge.
Git is native `git` + `gh` via bash — no separate VCS client. Per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE`: compress fires only on external-review approval («no comments»), never on internal CLEAN, never on a timer.
SddReviewLifecycle.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE
This role's bash commands stay within this list: - **Must run:** `sdd-verify --profile ` — MANDATORY, the ONE command that both fixes and verifies. It walks a fixed ladder for the WHOLE project (no path arguments; an extra positional argument or unknown flag is a hard error, `ERR_CLI_SDD_VERIFY_BAD_INVOCATION`, never a silent per-file scope): `type-check` → `test`/`test:coverage` (**foundation** — halts the ladder on failure, nothing later runs — no point polishing code that does not build or breaks tests) → `format:fix` → `lint:fix` (mutating repair, marker `🔧` — a failure here is a finding, not a halt) → `lint` → `format` (read-only, accumulate) → `yagni` (`full` only, `via gennady`). Profile composition is fixed per phase kind (STEP_5 names each set); only `full` has no repair rungs — a final verdict must never mutate the sources it judges. Runs before §5 commands, and is never repeated from §5 — that table holds only the EXTRA commands beyond this gate. **RUN-ALL — scoped to the gates AFTER the foundation**: once the foundation passes, every remaining gate runs regardless of an earlier non-halting failure; failures accumulate; repair rungs that rewrote files trigger one foundation re-run. An undeclared npm script is skipped with an honest `⏭` line — never an error, never silence — EXCEPT the foundation of `code`/`test`/`full`: required, so an absent or `echo`-stub script there is a red `⛔` (a phase must never pass on zero real checks) — not fixable from inside the phase: `BLOCKER_FORMAT` + `H_BLOCKED`. Gate subprocess output is suppressed on success; the CLI prints `ALL PASS` plus one marker line per gate (`✅` pass, `🔧` mutating, `⏭` skipped). Failed gates dump their command, exit code, and captured output. A foundation failure → fix in-zone, re-run the whole ladder; a non-halting failure → fix, re-run before EMIT_HANDOFF. Log each passing gate on a separate `ver` line. - **Must run:** verification commands from ticket §5 that match this phase's Rules (per `AX_VERIFICATION_BEFORE_HANDOFF`). - **May run:** `ls ` for targeted recon (NOT `-la` or recursive); `tsc --noEmit` after code changes; `node --test ` for test-kind phases; `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` for timestamps. - **May run:** `sdd-extract ` — extract anchored section from ticket/spec. - **May run:** `gennady lint --spec= ` — gennady DBC AST contract lint scoped to THIS phase's own files (closed-world inventory sync + cast safety); the one command in this list that actually accepts paths — use it, not `sdd-verify`, when the goal is "check only my own files".
Trust the context handed at dispatch — ticket, spec, manifest, diff — as current: it MUST be used as-is, not re-derived through bash. When a step in this directive names a real gap beyond what was handed (new commits since dispatch, a sibling branch, a file's history), `git`/`gh` reads (`status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `blame`, `gh pr view`/`diff`) are the legal way to close it. Mutating the repository (`git add`/`commit`/`push`/`rebase`/`reset`, `gh pr create`/`merge`) stays reserved for the step that owns publish/commit.
Absent such a step, treat `git`/`gh` as off the table: re-deriving handed context costs ~100-300ms per call for zero value, and full project recon / repository mutation belong to the orchestrator or authoring flow, not this role.
All recon stays inside the project root. A fact that genuinely lives outside it — a global `~/.npmrc`, a system-wide setting, anything outside this checkout — is not a gap this role closes by reading it anyway, read-only or not: no bash command in this list reaches outside the project root, and none should be improvised to. That fact is `H_BLOCKED` per `AX_BLOCKER_ESCALATION` with the specific question named — the operator is the channel for what the sandbox cannot see, not a last resort after trying anyway.
**Temp files stay under `.claude/tmp/`, nowhere else.** Any scratch or trial file this role needs — a throwaway script, an intermediate probe output — is created ONLY under `.claude/tmp/` inside the project root: create the directory when it does not yet exist, and remove what was created once it stops being needed (shared, reused across roles and other purposes — not this phase's private space to leave dirty). The system `/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`, and the repository root are closed for this: a root-level scratch file pollutes the diff and gets caught by the same inventory/lint gates meant for real `Target Files`, and `/tmp`/`$TMPDIR` sit outside the checkout this role's recon is scoped to above.
**Forbidden:** `npm run fix`; `npm run check`; `npm run lint` alone (overkill — use `sdd-verify` or `tsc --noEmit` for narrower checks); `npm run format`; `prettier` directly — repair and verification both live INSIDE `sdd-verify`, never called piecemeal; any recursive or project-wide file scan; any command that reads unrelated files for «context».
**One exemption from the Forbidden list — and only this.** A ticket §5 command (`npm run format` included) this phase must run verbatim (`AX_VERIFICATION_BEFORE_HANDOFF`: its `Required by` overlaps this phase's `Rules`) — `sdd-verify` itself is the sole self-initiated mutator, via its own internal `format:fix`/`lint:fix` rungs; no other self-initiated command here may write. Anything outside this one exemption — a self-initiated `npm run format`, `npm run fix`, a direct `prettier` call — stays forbidden. This exemption does not relax error-ownership: a §5 command reformatting or failing OUTSIDE this phase's Target Files is `BLOCKER_FORMAT` with a remediation proposal, never a mandate to format another phase's files.
SddReviewLifecycle.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_AWAITING_EXTERNAL_REVIEW` | Change published — session waits for the operator's verdict (feedback or «no comments»). A PAUSE, not a failure. | | `H_DIRTY_TREE_NOT_THIS_CHANGE` | The git working tree carries changes unrelated to this spec change — operator resolves before publish |

Step.Goal: Internal review until CLEAN — necessary, not sufficient.
Step.Action: Dispatch the critic (isolated), on a worker-tier model (`AX_CRITIC_MODEL_TIER`), on the review-state spec — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/critic.directive.xml")` (product / design lenses: completeness · implementation-autonomy · understanding · product-value). Apply its findings in place (still review-state — manifest + `✚`/`~`); loop until CLEAN.

Step.Goal: Publish the change for external review.
Step.Action: Verify the working tree carries ONLY this spec change (`git status`; else `H_DIRTY_TREE_NOT_THIS_CHANGE`). Commit the review-state spec on the working branch (`git add ` → `git commit`), `git push`, open the MR/PR (`gh pr create`) and capture its link — all via bash within `AX_PERMITTED_BASH_COMMANDS`. Present the MR link to the operator — the diff reads as a PR (Change Manifest + `✚`/`~` marks make the delta legible).
`H_AWAITING_EXTERNAL_REVIEW` — pause. The operator reviews the MR and returns with feedback or «no comments».
Feedback → apply edits in place (update the manifest + marks), `git push`, back to STEP_1 (re-critic → re-publish → await again). «no comments» (approved) → STEP_5.

Compress per `AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE`: remove the `CHANGE_MANIFEST` whole, strip the `✚`/`~` marks (lines stay), resolve any ID collisions in one commit, `pivot` → mark superseded decisions.
Decision Log semantic compression — the «Verdict → compress meaning» step, mandatory, runs over the spec's ENTIRE Decision Log (entries from before this change AND ones this change added, not only the new ones): classify every entry against `AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`'s test («could a future agent re-derive this from the spec's own tables/prose alone?»). Three outcomes, applied in the same commit as the rest of the compression: (a) **dissolve into the spec** — the entry is obvious/derivable (a tool pick the Tool Stack table already states, etc.); fold its substance into the section it belongs to if that section doesn't already carry it, then delete the DL entry; (b) **keep as DL** — a genuine compromise, rejected alternative, accepted risk, or rule exception the spec's tables/prose don't otherwise carry; leave it, unchanged; (c) **merge duplicates** — two or more entries reaching the same conclusion collapse into the surviving `D-NNN`, per `AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION` when one supersedes another. Report the tally in the compression summary shown to the operator: `Decision Log: растворено, оставлено, слито`.
`git commit` → `gh pr merge`. Then `sdd-check` on the spec MUST be clean of `SDD_REVIEW_STATE_STUCK` / `SDD_REVIEW_INCONSISTENT` (no manifest or marks remain). The spec is now master; return to the authoring flow's downstream handoff.

SddReviewLifecycle.HardForbidden: - Compressing on internal-critic CLEAN — compress waits for external approval (`AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE`). - Authoring spec content — the loading flow owns that; I only run critic / publish / compress. - Merging with the `CHANGE_MANIFEST` or `✚`/`~` marks still present — that is stuck review-state.
